prompt:
Turn Image 1 into a photorealistic photograph. Image 1 is an untextured 3D render of the real site and it fixes the exact composition: keep the same camera position, height, angle, lens and framing, the same horizon height, and keep every building, tree line, road, beach and landmark at the same position, size and outline. Do not move the camera. Do not move, add or remove buildings, do not change the number of floors, and do not add any landmark that is not in Image 1. Only replace the flat 3D surfaces with real materials, light and detail.

Layout of Image 1 to keep: an eye-level view, camera 2 m above the paving, looking along the coast. The paved plaza fills the bottom quarter and the horizon is at about 72% height. The towers are on the left: the nearest at 9–32% of the width with its roof 11% below the top edge, the second partly behind it at 26–41%, the third smaller at 36–47%. The right half of the frame is open sky above the beach and the promenade.

Málaga Towers by Estudio Lamela: three identical residential towers, each with exactly the number of floors shown in Image 1 (21 residential floors above the base). Every floor is ringed by thick bright-white cantilevered slab plates about one metre deep; their projection changes from floor to floor and from segment to segment, so each outline is a jagged stack of white bands with deep shadow beneath every plate, never neat identical rings. Frameless clear glass balustrades on every plate; recessed dark grey-blue floor-to-ceiling glazing; grey horizontal-slat louvre panels in some bays. The base: a recessed dark-glass ground floor under a deep white overhang, then a wide continuous white band with a row of straight vertical white posts. Flat roof with a dark graphite plant room.

Visible, exactly where Image 1 shows it: the wide light-grey paved promenade plaza with rows of tall palm trees and tall white lamp posts; the road with trees on the left; the golden beach on the right; the tall pale-brick Los Guindos chimney small in the distance just right of centre; low mountains on the horizon.

Golden hour a few minutes before sunset: a low warm sun from the west-south-west lights the sea-facing facades and the white plates a warm golden apricot, with a crisp dark shadow under every plate; faces turned away from the sun are soft cool blue; clear pale-blue sky warming to peach near the horizon, soft haze over the sea. Photoreal architectural photograph, natural colour, crisp detail, no people in focus, no text or logos, 16:9.
